glosses: S’empêcher de faire quelque chose ; se priver de l’usage de quelque chose.

examples.text: Les podagres doivent-ils s’abstenir entièrement de vin ? Il y a un axiome populaire qui dit : buvez ou ne buvez pas de vin, et vous n'en aurez pas moins la goutte.
Nous nous étions abstenus de faire du feu dans la crainte que la fumée ne révélât notre présence, mais voyant que nous étions découverts, nous fîmes la cuisine.
Le metsulfuron est dégradé uniquement à pH acide. […]. Il convient donc d’être prudent et de s’abstenir de modifier les caractéristiques de pH de la bouillie.

glosses: Ne pas voter lors d’un scrutin.
Décider de ne pas faire ce qu’on fait normalement.

examples.text: Ce juge s’abstient d’opiner, de juger ou simplement Ce juge s’abstient : il se récuse lui-même.
Cet héritier s’est abstenu de la succession, Il n’a pas fait acte d’héritier.
La forte tempête a abstenu les marins de sortir en mer.

glosses: Refrain from (something or doing something); keep from doing, especially an indulgence.

examples.text: In order to improve his health, Rob decided to abstain from smoking.

The Security Council […] calls upon all Governments and authorities, without prejudice to the rights, claims or positions of the parties concerned, to abstain from any hostile military action in Palestine and to that end to issue a cease-fire order to their military and paramilitary forces
Who abstains from meat that is not gaunt?

glosses: Deliberately refrain from casting one's vote at a meeting where one is present.

examples.text: I abstain from this vote, as I have no particular preference.
[…]forcing a small portion of the population to abstain from voting
Whether he abstain men from marying [sic].

glosses: To avoid; to shun, to shy away from.

examples.text:
And peraduenture my lady the quene sente for hym to that entente that syr Launcelot shold come to her good grace pryuely and secretely wenynge to her that hit was best so to do in eschewyng & dredyng of sklaunder
"And peradventure my lady, the queen, sent for him to that intent that Sir Launcelot should come to her good grace privily and secretly, weening to her that it was best so to do, in eschewing and dreading of slander"
What cannot be eschew'd must be embrac'd.
Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.
Above all, let her eschew the impertinence of invention; let her leave genius to her milliner.

He could afford no servants, and would admit but few visitors to his absolute solitude; eschewing close friendships and receiving his rare acquaintances in one of the three ground-floor rooms which he kept in order.

[S]he [Edwina, mother of Tennessee Williams] was indeed Amanda [Wingfield, character in Williams' play The Glass Menagerie] in the flesh: a doughty chatterbox from Ohio who adopted the manner of a Southern belle and eschewed both drink and sex to the greatest extent possible.
I eschew the idea of plugging in my laptop to take notes and resort to old-fashioned pen and paper instead, so that I can enjoy more of the view and not be distracted by bashing a keyboard.

glosses: No tomar una acción, evitar hacer algo.
No participar en una decisión o acción.
non intervenire nell'andamento di qualcosa, nel suo processo
decidere di non votare, diritto nei paesi democratici ed in alcuni altri
